summary.text: Bryan Cutler represents the 100th Legislative District in Lancaster County in the Pennsylvania House of Representatives and is serving his eighth term.
He was elected 139th Speaker of the House in June 2020, became Minority Leader for the 2023-24 session, and is the Republican chairman of the House Education Committee for 2025-26.

paragraphs.text: Cutler is a lifelong resident of the Peach Bottom area, according to his official biography, which says both of his parents were diagnosed with ALS while he was in high school and that he cared for them and his younger sister.
He put himself through trade school to become an X-ray technologist, then graduated summa cum laude from Lebanon Valley College with a health care management degree.

After several years overseeing budgets and operations in a hospital radiology department, he earned a law degree focused on health care law from Widener Law School and practiced with the firm of Nikolaus & Hohenadel.
He was first elected in 2006 and previously served as Majority Leader before his election as Speaker, and he was re-elected Speaker on January 5, 2021.

The biography says he was the prime sponsor of legislation that led to Act 164 of 2012, on fraud detection in the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, and Act 60 of 2013, on hospital accreditation procedures.
In 2019, it says, his bill funded new trauma centers in rural Pennsylvania.
Cutler and his wife, Jennifer, have three children and live on an 11-acre hobby farm in the log cabin home where he grew up, and the family attends Wrightsdale Baptist Church.
